title: Back and Forward history menus: right-click a button to jump several folders at once
problem: The history keeps full back and forward stacks (src/model.rs:119-173), but the only way through them is one step at a time: `go_back`/`go_forward` (src/finder/mod.rs:960-973) from the two toolbar buttons (src/finder/toolbar.rs:315-331), the keys, or the mouse's side buttons. The buttons have no menu and their tooltips are just 'Back' and 'Forward' (toolbar.rs:318, 326), so there is no way to see where Back leads or to return five folders in one go. Finder (click and hold), Explorer (recent locations) and browsers (right-click) all list the history on these buttons.
proposal: model.rs: add `History::back_list()` and `forward_list()` (nearest first) and `go_back_by(n)`/`go_forward_by(n)` that pop n times. mod.rs: `Finder::go_back_by(steps, window, cx)` and the forward twin, each calling `end_search` and `location_changed` once, as `go_back` does; `go_back` becomes `go_back_by(1)`. toolbar.rs: wrap each nav button in a stateful `div().id("back-history")` with `.context_menu(..)` (gpui-component's `ContextMenuExt`, already used at src/finder/tab_bar.rs:378) listing up to about 12 `Location::title()` entries, each `window.listener_for(&view, move |this, _, window, cx| this.go_back_by(n, window, cx))`. An empty menu is never shown (see src/finder/menus.rs:380-381), so nothing appears without history. Name the destination in the tooltip: 'Back to Projects'. Document at docs/manual.md:179.
original_test_plan: Unit test in src/model.rs: navigate A, B, C; `back_list()` is [B, A]; `go_back_by(2)` leaves current A with forward [B, C] and `can_back()` false. Headless UI test beside `back_and_forward_buttons` (tests/controls.rs:38): `ui.go_to(Projects)`, `ui.go_to(Projects/atlas)`, `ui.right_click("back")`, assert `menu_labels()` is [Projects, <fixture folder name>], click the second, assert `ui.folder() == fx.dir`; then `ui.right_click("forward")` lists [Projects, atlas].
original_risks: On Linux windows without server decorations a right-click in the toolbar also opens the window menu (toolbar.rs:193-197); the nav pill's right-click must not reach that handler. Two history entries can share a title (two folders named `src`); showing the tildified parent path beside the name would tell them apart. Shares toolbar.rs with split-view-toolbar-clip and tooltip-shortcuts, and the History type with back-forward-restore-search (entries that carry a search would need a label).

verifier.claim_check:
The described behaviour is true. History keeps both stacks (src/model.rs:119-123) but only steps one entry at a time: back()/forward() pop once (model.rs:149-165) and nothing exposes the lists. Finder::go_back/go_forward (src/finder/mod.rs:960-973) are the only callers, reached from the toolbar buttons (src/finder/toolbar.rs:315-331, fixed tooltips "Back"/"Forward" at 318 and 326), the keys (src/actions.rs:137-140), the Go menu (actions.rs:406-407), the action handlers (mod.rs:3057-3058) and the mouse side buttons (mod.rs:3149-3160). I found no other history list (no recent-folders menu, nothing in the server protocol). docs/manual.md:179 documents stepping only, CHANGELOG.md has nothing on it, and no test pins the absence (tests/controls.rs:38-60 and tests/basics.rs:235-248 only step).

Three points in the proposal do not hold against gpui-component 0.8.1:
1. "An empty menu is never shown, so nothing appears without history" is only half true. ContextMenu skips drawing an empty menu (menu/context_menu.rs:310), but open_menu still moves focus into it (context_menu.rs:505). An undrawn menu can never be dismissed, and fffinder has no focus-lost recovery, so right-clicking Back in a fresh window would leave the keyboard dead until the next click.
2. A right-click on an enabled Button focuses the button: GPUI focuses a focus-tracked element on any mouse-down (gpui-pre-0.3.10/src/elements/div.rs:2826-2839) and Button suppresses that for the left button only (button/button.rs:857-870). The menu records that as the focus to restore (context_menu.rs:427-435, popup_menu.rs:1074-1091), so after the menu closes the keyboard sits on the Back button, not the files. A left click on Back does not do this.
3. The listed Linux window-menu risk is already handled. ContextMenu's right-mouse-down listener calls cx.stop_propagation() (context_menu.rs:402-406) and is registered after the toolbar's handler (toolbar.rs:193-197), so it runs first. The comment at src/finder/menus.rs:380 saying menus don't stop propagation is stale.
verifier.implementation_notes:
The proposal's shape is right; apply it with the corrections below.

**src/model.rs (History)**
- Add `back_list()` and `forward_list()` returning `impl Iterator<Item = &Location>`, nearest first. Both stacks keep the nearest entry last, so each is `.iter().rev()`.
- Add `back_by(steps) -> bool` and `forward_by(steps) -> bool`, all or nothing: return false when `steps == 0 || steps > len`, otherwise run the existing single-step body `steps` times. This makes a stale menu entry a no-op if history changes while the menu is open.
- Keep `back()`/`forward()` as `*_by(1)`; the unit tests at model.rs:391-458 use them.

**src/finder/mod.rs**
- Add `pub fn go_back_by(&mut self, steps: usize, window, cx)`: call `end_search`, then if `history.back_by(steps)`, call `location_changed(select, ..)` once.
- Use `select = self.history.forward_list().next().and_then(Location::folder).map(Path::to_path_buf)`. For one step this equals today's `from`, so "back selects the folder we left" (tests/controls.rs:53-57) still holds. For longer jumps it selects the folder entered from the destination.
- Add `go_forward_by` likewise with `location_changed(None, ..)`.
- `go_back(&GoBack, ..)` and `go_forward(&GoForward, ..)` keep their signatures (they are action handlers at mod.rs:3057-3058 and called at 3152, 3158 and toolbar.rs:321, 329) and delegate with 1.

**src/finder/toolbar.rs**
- Import `ContextMenuExt as _`.
- Wrap each nav button as the codebase already does elsewhere (sidebar.rs:753-756, bars.rs:282-287): `div().id("back-history").flex_none().child(button).context_menu(move |menu, window, cx| history_menu(&view, menu, forward, window, cx))`, and the same for `"forward-history"`.
- Always wrap; do not add or remove the wrapper as history comes and goes. ContextMenu adds an element id to the button's path and Button keys its focus handle by that path (button/button.rs:652-657), so toggling it would drop focus from a keyboard-activated Back button.
- On each nav Button (it implements InteractiveElement), add `.on_mouse_down(MouseButton::Right, move |_, window, cx| { window.prevent_default(); if !has_history { cx.stop_propagation(); } })`.
  - `prevent_default` is the trick Button uses for the left button: the right-click no longer focuses the button, so the menu restores focus to the files.
  - `stop_propagation` when the stack is empty keeps the click from ContextMenu, so the undrawn, focus-stealing empty menu never opens. The button's listeners are registered after ContextMenu's (context_menu.rs:399-411), so they run first in the bubble phase.
- No extra code is needed for the Linux window menu.
- `history_menu`: read `view.read(cx).history`, clone up to about 12 locations nearest first (PopupMenu turns scrollable past 20 items, popup_menu.rs:823). For entry `ix`, add `PopupMenuItem::new(label).on_click(window.listener_for(view, move |this: &mut Finder, _: &ClickEvent, window, cx| this.go_back_by(ix + 1, window, cx)))`. Finish with `.min_w(ui(200.))`.
- Build labels in a pure function: `Location::title()`, and only where two shown entries share a title, append the parent as `format!("{title} — {}", super::tildify(parent))` (`tildify` is at mod.rs:191). Plain titles otherwise keep the UI test simple.
- Tooltips come from a pure helper: `Back to “Projects”` in the quote style of toolbar.rs:420, plain "Back"/"Forward" when there is nowhere to go. If the tooltip-shortcuts candidate lands first, keep its call and change only the text.

**Docs**
- Extend the Back, Forward row at docs/manual.md:179.
- Add a bullet under "Toolbar menus" (manual.md:842-847).
- Add an entry under CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] → Added.
verifier.test_plan:
Everything runs headless on Linux.

**Unit test in src/model.rs** (`mod tests`, next to `history_back_forward`)
- Navigate A, B, C; `back_list()` is [B, A].
- `back_by(3)` returns false and changes nothing.
- `back_by(2)` leaves current A, `forward_list()` is [B, C], `can_back()` is false.
- `forward_by(2)` returns to C.

**Unit test in src/finder/toolbar.rs** (`mod tests`, next to `the_toolbar_folds_one_step_at_a_time`)
- The pure label helper: two entries with the same folder name get their parent appended; unique names stay plain.
- The pure tooltip helper: `Back to “Projects”` with history, "Back" without. Button tooltips are not observable through the harness, so this must be a unit test.

**UI test in tests/controls.rs**, beside `back_and_forward_buttons` (line 38), using `Fixture::new`, `Ui::open`, and the helpers in tests/common/mod.rs:
1. Fresh window: `ui.right_click("back")`, then assert `!ui.menu_open()` and `ui.files_focused()`. This pins the empty-menu focus trap.
2. `ui.go_to(&fx.path("Projects"))`, `ui.go_to(&fx.path("Projects/atlas"))`, `ui.right_click("back")`. Assert `ui.menu_labels() == ["Projects", Location::Folder(fx.dir.clone()).title()]`.
3. `ui.click_menu_item(<fixture name>)`. Assert `ui.folder() == Some(fx.dir.clone())`, `ui.selected() == ["Projects"]`, `!ui.read(|f| f.can_go_back())`, `!ui.menu_open()` and `ui.files_focused()`. The last pins the right-click-focuses-the-button problem.
4. `ui.right_click("forward")`. Assert `ui.menu_labels() == ["Projects", "atlas"]`. `ui.press("escape")`, assert `ui.files_focused()`.
5. Reopen, `ui.click_menu_item("atlas")`, assert `ui.folder() == Some(fx.path("Projects/atlas"))`.

`ui.right_click("back")` still finds the button inside the wrapper, because the harness matches the last id of the element path (gpui-base test_support.rs:232-236).

**Existing tests that must stay green**
- `back_and_forward_buttons` (tests/controls.rs:38)
- `the_mouse_back_and_forward_buttons_navigate` (tests/basics.rs:235)
- `the_toolbar_folds_just_when_the_drawn_controls_run_out_of_room` (tests/basics.rs:574); this one fails if the wrapper changes the pill's width.
verifier.risks:
- **Focus regressions if the two guards are omitted.** An empty menu takes the keyboard for good, and a right-click parks focus on the Back button. Both are pinned by `files_focused()` assertions in the UI test.
- **Toolbar width arithmetic.** The wrapper divs must not change the nav pill's width (toolbar.rs:27-50); tests/basics.rs:574 measures it.
- **Linux without server decorations.** The two nav buttons stop passing right-clicks through to the window menu. The manual only promises that for empty toolbar space (docs/manual.md:186), so this is acceptable.
- **Low discoverability.** Right-click on a button is hidden; only the tooltip and manual surface it. Value is modest because path-bar crumbs already jump several ancestors at once. That is why I rate it 2, not 3.
- **Merge overlap.** toolbar.rs is shared with split-view-toolbar-clip and tooltip-shortcuts (same tooltip lines); History is shared with back-forward-restore-search, whose entries would need their own labels.
- **Stale entries.** If history changes while a menu is open (for example a remote `fff show`), the entry indexes are stale. The all-or-nothing `*_by` makes that a no-op instead of a wrong jump.
- **Not verified by running.** I did not run cargo; the event-order and focus conclusions come from reading gpui-pre 0.3.10 and gpui-component 0.8.1 sources.

orchestrator_notes: 'tooltip-shortcuts' lands before this one and changes the Back and Forward tooltips; build on it.
